stem: A person suddenly develops one-sided facial weakness and trouble speaking. Which of the following actions should a nearby person take?

options.label: A
options.text: Offer water and watch for improvement
options.misconception: Observation is being chosen despite a time-sensitive stroke warning pattern.
options.explanation: The CDC advises calling emergency services right away rather than waiting to see whether sudden stroke symptoms improve.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask the person to sleep briefly
options.misconception: Rest is being substituted for urgent assessment of sudden focal neurologic symptoms.
options.explanation: Sleep delays emergency evaluation; the cited action for sudden one-sided weakness or speech trouble is an immediate emergency call.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; suspected stroke symptoms require an immediate emergency call.
options.explanation: Sudden unilateral facial weakness and trouble speaking are stroke warning signs. The CDC directs bystanders to call emergency services right away.

options.label: D
options.text: Arrange a routine clinic visit later
options.misconception: A routine timeline is being applied to an acute neurologic emergency.
options.explanation: A later appointment is inappropriate for this sudden pattern; the cited response is to call emergency services immediately.

options.label: E
options.text: Let the person drive to hospital
options.misconception: Self-transport is being chosen instead of activating emergency medical help.
options.explanation: The CDC advises an immediate emergency call so medical personnel can begin care during transport rather than having the affected person drive.

context: Learning objective: act on suspected stroke. New one-sided weakness or speech difficulty is time-sensitive; activate emergency medical services immediately.
